risks: Low: changes to how an existing public health service is delivered. Home blood draw carries the usual small risks of venepuncture; privacy risk if contact information leaves the program.
consent: Contact evaluation is a public health service; contacts consent to each test as now. Program evaluation uses de-identified extracts under the data steward's approval.
data: Contact names stay in the case management system; the extract (DS-114) holds dates and contact type only.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: people in shelters, shift workers, people needing interpreters and people without a phone are the least likely to complete evaluation. The redesign books interpreters for every step, offers evening home visits and shelter-based blood draws, and reports completion for these groups separately each quarter.
effectiveness: Success is a sustained rise to at least 85 percent with no fall for the hardest-to-reach contacts.
efficiency: Removes two handoffs and repeated calls; nurse visit time rises.
costs: Courier pickups within the existing contract; staff time.
partnerships: Shelter staff, a community interpreter service, hospital radiology booking and two people who went through contact evaluation last year.
rebPath: Program evaluation under the medical officer of health's approval (MOH-TB-2026-05) with de-identified data; not research requiring REB review, and a publication would follow SQUIRE 2.0.
limitations: Before-and-after within one program; radiology booking outside program control.
summary: Low-risk service redesign with de-identified evaluation data and equity reporting.
